label: a private coachman standing in his livery, 1900s
note: Gathered 2026-11-07 for T-3483, Charles Nelson's standing livery. The coachman_1904 set shows coachmen on the box; this one shows a coachman on foot, full length, in the livery he stood in. Neither plate is of Chicago or of Nelson: a reference set says what a man of this role and decade looked like, not what Nelson wore. Both are monochrome halftones and say nothing about colour.

pictures.name: seely_1902_coachman
pictures.from: Internet Archive scan mrsseelyscookboo00seel, leaf n68 (2394 x 3503) turned upright, crop [2050, 0, 3400, 2150]: the right-hand figure of the plate, at full resolution
pictures.caption: Coachman standing in livery, full length. Mrs. Seely's Cook Book (New York, 1902), plate facing p. 26
pictures.shows: A clean-shaven coachman full length from the front at a few metres: double-breasted coat buttoned to the throat and falling to the knee, two rows of six bright buttons, white stock, white gloves, white breeches above black top boots, silk hat, a long whip in his right hand.

pictures.name: seely_1902_mourning
pictures.from: Internet Archive scan mrsseelyscookboo00seel, leaf n72 (2394 x 3503) turned upright, crop [450, 0, 1750, 2150]: the left-hand figure of the plate, at full resolution
pictures.caption: Older coachman in mourning livery, full length. Mrs. Seely's Cook Book (New York, 1902), plate facing p. 28
pictures.shows: An older, heavier coachman full length from the front: the same double-breasted coat cut to mid-calf, two rows of buttons, dark gloves, dark trousers and boots, silk hat; clean-shaven.

pictures.caption: Carriage footman and coachman side by side. Mrs. Seely's Cook Book (New York, 1902), plate facing p. 26
pictures.shows: The two liveried men whole and small on the page: how the coat, the white breeches and the black boots read as blocks at a distance, the coat's bright buttons as two dotted lines.
